$schema_note: Controlled characteristic vocabulary. Traits are grouped into four top-level families. Each trait has a stable id, a display name, a one-line definition, and a canonical example game. This is a stub; groups and traits will expand during vocabulary design.

tone_theme.name: Tone & Theme
tone_theme.description: The emotional register and subject matter a game evokes.

traits.name: Melancholic
traits.definition: A pervasive wistful sadness that colors the world and its story.

traits.name: Cozy
traits.definition: Low-stakes, comforting play that prioritizes warmth over tension.

traits.name: Existential
traits.definition: Foregrounds questions of meaning, mortality, and identity.

mechanics.name: Mechanics
mechanics.description: The core interactive systems the player operates.

traits.name: Deckbuilding
traits.definition: Players assemble and refine a deck of cards as the primary progression loop.

traits.name: Immersive Sim
traits.definition: Systemic worlds where interacting rules permit many valid solutions.

traits.name: Permadeath
traits.definition: Death is permanent, resetting progress and raising the weight of each choice.

traits.name: Painterly
traits.definition: Hand-painted textures and brushwork evoking traditional media.

traits.name: Diegetic UI
traits.definition: Interface elements exist inside the fiction rather than overlaying it.

structure.name: Structure
structure.description: How play is organized across time and space.

traits.name: Metroidvania
traits.definition: An interconnected map gated by abilities, rewarding backtracking.

traits.name: Run-Based
traits.definition: Play is divided into discrete attempts with meta-progression between them.

traits.name: Open World
traits.definition: A large continuous space explorable in a largely non-linear order.
traits.example_game: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
